measures.questionText: Shall a charter study commission be created to study the WRITE-IN SPACE ONLY present governmental structure of Barnstable County to consider and make findings concerning the form of government and make recommendations thereon?
measures.officialStatement:
Question A will appear on ballots in all 15 Barnstable County towns in the November 2026 election.

If Question A passes countywide, a 19-member Charter Study Commission would be created. It would include 15 elected representatives — one from each Barnstable County town — plus three County Commissioners or their designees and the Speaker of the Assembly of Delegates or her designee.

Candidates elected as Charter Study Commissioners will take office only if Question A passes countywide.

The 15 elected town representatives would have population-weighted votes, meaning their voting strength on the Commission would be based on the population of the town they represent.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Creates a commission to study Barnstable County’s current government structure and recommend changes to its form of government. If approved countywide, the commission would have 19 members: one elected representative from each of the county’s 15 towns, the three County Commissioners or their designees, and the Assembly of Delegates’ Speaker or her designee. The 15 elected town representatives would have votes weighted by their towns’ populations. The separately elected charter-study commissioners would take office only if Question A passes. The question creates a study commission to make findings and recommendations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not create the proposed charter-study commission.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Falmouth to collect property taxes above Proposition 2½’s normal limits for the amounts needed to pay bonds for replacing the East Falmouth Library at 310 East Falmouth Highway. The covered work includes demolishing the existing building, designing and building the new library, landscaping, paving, utilities and other site improvements, storage and moving expenses, furnishings, equipment, and related costs. The exclusion applies to the bond payments for this project.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the property-tax debt exclusion for these library project bond payments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed debt exclusion for these library project bond payments.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Needham to collect property taxes above Proposition 2½’s normal limits for the amounts needed to pay bonds for a new Pollard Middle School on Harris Avenue. The covered costs include architectural design, engineering, construction, demolition and site work, including related costs. The exclusion applies to the bond payments for this school project.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the property-tax debt exclusion for these Pollard Middle School bond payments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed debt exclusion for these school project bond payments.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Swansea to collect property taxes above Proposition 2½’s normal limits for the amounts needed to pay bonds for a new school building and related site work at Joseph Case High School, 70 School Street. The question describes a building of about 114,707 square feet designed for 510 students in grades 6 through 8. The exclusion applies to the bond payments for this project.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the property-tax debt exclusion for these school construction bond payments.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject the proposed debt exclusion for these school construction bond payments.
